sources.citation: Holmer, Nils M. 1983. Linguistic survey of south-eastern Queensland. Pacific Linguistics D-54. Canberra: ANU. Part II 'The languages of the Gunggari group', 2.11, p. 178; Bidjara section p. 205.
sources.note: Group-level only, Wadja/Wadjigu never named in the volume (grep = 0): 'Word or syllable stress is not significant in any of the languages studied here... in a spoken context or sequence of syllables, however, the second initial syllable often carries mechanically more stress than the others' (p. 178); for Bidjara p. 205: 'Neither is word stress [distinctive]... a certain tendency exists... to accentuate the second initial syllable, with secondary stress appearing on subsequent alternate syllables'. Neighbouring-group evidence (Gunggari, Bidjara, Marganj, Gangulu, Wirri, Birri), not a Wadjigu…

sources.citation: Curr, Edward M. (ed.). 1887. The Australian Race, vol. III. Melbourne: John Ferres, Government Printer. No. 156 'Nogoa River' (Thomas Middleton and E. Irving Noble, pp. 90-95) and No. 157 'Head of the Comet River' (Thomas Josephson, 'Kanoloo tribe', pp. 96-99).
sources.note: Nothing. Prefatory ethnographic notes plus English-Aboriginal vocabulary only; grep for accent/stress/emphasis/pronunciation over pp. 90-99 gives zero hits. These are the only Wadjigu-tagged items in Glottolog that are open online (Glottolog: Middleton = Gara-Gara = Wadjigu; Josephson's Kanoloo = Ganulu = Wadjigu).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page wadj1255 and reference pages 4842, 77072; hh.bib (Glottolog bibliography, on file).
sources.note: Nothing. Confirms: no grammar/phonology/sketch for Wadjigu (n_glottolog_desc_refs = 0); only Breen 2009, Terrill 1993, the two Curr 1887 wordlists and non-descriptive misc items are tagged wdu. Alternative names Maudalgo, Wadja, Wadjainggo, Wadju, Wadya, Waindjago, Wainggo, Wainjago, Wainjigo, Watjigu.
Nothing on stress or accent; lists Wadjingu among Bidjara dialects (attribution from the State Library of Queensland languages map) and gives only vowel/consonant inventories from Breen 1973/1981.

sources.note: Google Books snippet: 'Bidyara/Gungabula (Breen 1973)... Main stress is initial. Secondary stress on odd nonfinal syllables, e.g. 10, 100, 1020, 10200, 102020'. This is Bidyara (bidy1243), a neighbouring Maric language of which Wikipedia (citing the SLQ languages map) treats Wadjingu as a dialect; Glottolog and AIATSIS keep Wadjigu separate. Not a Wadjigu statement.
